core.title: Map each telemetry URN to its directory of signal files
core.given: A plan artifact, wagon or acceptance declares telemetry URNs, or work touches, validates or generates from files in the telemetry signal tree.
core.when: You author, edit, rename or validate a telemetry URN, its signal files, or the manifest built from them.
core.then: Keep each telemetry URN's signals in the signal directory derived from that URN, as signal files named {signal-type}.{plane}[.{measure}] with the profile's signal-file suffix, carrying a measure on metric signals and none on event signals.
prefer: Derive the signal directory's path segments from the URN's theme and segment separators.
Name metric signal files with their measure component and event signal files without one.
Planes: ui, ux, be, nw, db, st, tm, sc, au, fn, if. Measures: count, duration, latency, size, rate, percentage.
avoid: Metric signal files without a measure component.
Event signal files with a measure component.
Planes or measures outside the controlled lists.
Hand-editing the telemetry manifest; it is generated from the profile's manifest input.
core.why: A deterministic URN-to-directory mapping lets tooling resolve URNs to signal files and generate the manifest from the filesystem; the signal type (quantitative metric vs discrete event) decides whether a measure is needed.
evidence: Every declared telemetry URN resolves to an existing signal directory derived from it.
Each file in that directory matches the signal-file name pattern, with the measure present if and only if the signal type is metric.
Plane and measure tokens are members of the controlled lists.
The telemetry manifest is generated from the profile's manifest input (not hand-authored).
verification: Resolve every declared telemetry URN to its signal directory using the profile's telemetry URN shape and signal-directory pattern, treating the URN's theme and segment separators (including the separator inside segments) as directory levels; a declared URN with no existing matching directory is a finding.

Check every file in each signal directory against the profile's signal-file name pattern; the measure component must be present exactly when the signal type is metric (metric signals require it, event signals must not carry it).

Check plane and measure tokens for membership in the controlled axes: planes ui, ux, be, nw, db, st, tm, sc, au, fn, if; measures (metric signals only) count, duration, latency, size, rate, percentage.
Check that the telemetry manifest is generated from the profile's manifest input rather than hand-authored; the rule does not require a committed manifest or a freshness check.

Recognize the telemetry signal tree by location: any file under the tree root glob supplied by the profile is an activation signal by itself, regardless of whether it is a recognized signal file; the detector also reports pre-existing noncompliance, not only changes introduced by the current task.

Task terms are candidate signals only; they confirm and activate the rule when a telemetry URN, a path under the telemetry signal tree (any file in the tree, per the profile's tree root glob), or telemetry manifest generation is in scope.

fires: A wagon or acceptance declares, edits or renames a telemetry URN
A signal file is added, renamed or removed under the telemetry signal tree
A task validates or reviews existing telemetry URNs, their signal directories or signal filenames
An existing telemetry URN has no matching signal directory
An existing signal file uses a plane or measure outside the controlled lists, a metric lacks a measure, or an event carries one
The telemetry manifest is generated or its generation input is changed
doesNotFire: Plan edits that declare no telemetry URNs, touch nothing under the telemetry signal tree and do not involve the telemetry manifest
Non-telemetry artifact URNs (covered by the general artifact-naming grammar)
A task merely mentioning the words 'event' or 'metric' with no telemetry URN, telemetry signal-tree path or manifest in scope

neutralityNotes: The concrete telemetry scheme data — the URN shape (telemetry:{theme}:{segments}), the signal-tree root glob (telemetry/**), the per-URN signal-directory pattern (telemetry/{theme}/{segments}/), the signal-file name pattern with its .json suffix ({signal-type}.{plane}[.{measure}].json) and the manifest generation input (telemetry/{domain}/{resource}/*.json) — is stack realization data; none of the closed vocabulary's keys fits, so it is carried by five proposed profile keys (urn.telemetry, layout.telemetry_signal_tree, layout.telemetry_signal_dir, suffix.telemetry_signal, layout.telemetry_manifest_input). Path-based activation is preserved as its own core fact: any file under the telemetry signal tree is an activation signal by location, independent of signal-file recognition, and a path under the tree also confirms candidate task terms (core:verification and doesNotFire); the tree location itself is profile data, so under the Bun profile it instantiates to telemetry/**. The controlled plane/measure lists stay in the core because they are ATDD scheme vocabulary, not stack structure. The OpenTelemetry-metric / analytics-event glosses remain Bun-only wording. The worked mapping example (verifier_detail[4]) and the legacy '{domain}/{resource}' manifest wording are not repeated in the core: bun.json remains the reference example, and the legacy wording survives only as the bunValue of layout.telemetry_manifest_input. Term ids (signal_type, telemetry_axes) are realization details named in core:verification only generically.
